summary: Apocrypha 1.0 web/PWA release candidate 1 is installable from supported desktop and mobile browsers and passed local desktop Chrome, Pixel-class Chrome, and iPhone 15 Pro WebKit checks covering owner access, manifest identity, service-worker scope, offline encrypted continuity, no private API caching, accessibility, safe areas, and overflow. It is not a native mobile binary or a production release; physical-device install, live-revision, and phone-to-desktop acceptance remain open.
objective: Keep Apocrypha useful, local, private, evidence-linked, and quietly alive between prompts while every external effect remains governed.
principles: Local operation remains useful when network access is removed.
Memory, claims, and actions retain source and authority boundaries.
Unavailable capabilities remain visibly degraded instead of simulated.
Public distribution waits for integrity, signature, install, rollback, and privacy proof.

milestones.label: 1.0 cross-platform web/PWA
milestones.summary: Version 1.0.0-rc.1 is an installable browser-delivered PWA candidate. The local matrix passed desktop Chrome, Pixel-class Chrome, and iPhone 15 Pro WebKit checks for access, manifest identity, service-worker scope, offline encrypted continuity, private-cache exclusion, accessibility, safe areas, and overflow. It is not an App Store, Play Store, desktop-native, or downloadable package, and production has not been promoted.

milestones.label: Personal Brain
milestones.summary: The simplified public shell, owner gate, and row-secured Mneme schema are live. Candidate 6 adds an explicit, authenticated, idempotent first-owner bootstrap instead of creating a profile silently; live owner creation and readback remain acceptance gates.

milestones.label: Mobile mini Brain and desktop sync
milestones.summary: The 1.0 PWA candidate includes an AES-GCM device-local vault, deterministic no-model recall and refusal, an installable offline shell, signed cursor and outbox synchronization, replay and conflict controls, and a restricted desktop relay. Desktop Chrome, Pixel-class Chrome, and iPhone 15 Pro WebKit checks passed locally; no physical-phone or end-to-end phone-to-desktop claim has been made.

milestones.label: Conversation constellations
milestones.summary: A privacy-safe aggregate exposes corpus scale and curated constellations without publishing raw conversation bodies; every held record remains unavailable until individual review and approval.

milestones.label: Humanity source admission
milestones.summary: A digest-bound admission gate separates reputation, factual trust, and human value while quarantining testimony and rejecting prohibited material.

milestones.label: Causal interoception and recovery
milestones.summary: Redacted causal traces, stable errors, stage latency fields, differential backups, and restore verification are implemented in the compatibility runtime.

milestones.label: CSL, NIL, and CSSL native core
milestones.summary: CSLv3 defines the contract, NIL defines the ordered timing graph, and CSSLv3 is the compiled target. The hardened native context frame is 1,780 tokenizer tokens, but the first canary exposed missing child-exit evidence; semantic parity, executable CSSLv3 policy, latency, and stable canary gates remain open.

milestones.label: Own executable language stack
milestones.summary: An authored artifact must change bounded behavior through a verified compiler or runtime to count. The first proofs are context selection, Graphify traversal, and mobile reconciliation under one inspectable NIL trace, with plain-language CSLv3 expansion and rollback.

milestones.label: Trinity-native cognitive organs
milestones.summary: Graphify is the first differential replacement. A read-only Rust query and path slice preserved exact fixed-query results, retained the Python oracle's morphology results, reduced cold-start cost, and proved that a sealed CSSLv3 policy changes bounded traversal while emitting a non-authoritative NIL trace. Product integration and a self-hosted CSSLv3 compiler remain open.

milestones.label: Signed local distribution
milestones.summary: A reversible Windows migration package exists and passed focused checks, but remains withheld pending native cryptographic signing, SBOM, and clean-machine lifecycle proof.

release_boundary: This plan is a public-safe projection of the 1.0 web/PWA candidate. It is not a deployment receipt, production acceptance result, native-app claim, or release announcement.
